sonnet.problem: The question says some will be "carried on the arm," which rules out the wrong answers "old prophets" and "first kings." Nobody carries those on the arm, so only "sons and daughters" is left.
sonnet.rule: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

sonnet.problem: Card 10 already tells "gold instead of bronze," so "Bronze" is the one metal the baker has seen. The other answers, Tin and Lead, are new. The right answer is given away by an earlier card.
sonnet.rule: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

sonnet.problem: Card 16 already says "their kings will serve her." Card 3 and card 16 have both put kings in front of the baker, so "Their kings" is an easy pick over priests and armies.
sonnet.rule: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

sonnet.problem: The statement puts Zion's children "on the ships of Tarshish." The text only says the ships of Tarshish are in the lead to bring them. It doesn't say the children sail on those ships. It also describes Tarshish as "a faraway land across the sea," which the text doesn't say.
sonnet.rule: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

sonnet.problem: The joke says Papa Dorin "started out on one kitchen counter." His backstory says he started out in a bin at a closing neighborhood bakery. His jokes may add small moments but must fit the backstory.
sonnet.rule: They fit the backstory, never change it, and don't contradict each other in one lesson.
